title: Composer dependency OSV advisory matches
review_note: Advisory match is actionable; severity should follow the matched advisory and affected version, not only static critical requirement severity. Lock metadata is not installed-byte attestation.

review_note: Security patch gap is actionable when product/version/release coverage is complete. Prioritize using the relevant bulletin rather than blanket critical.

title: Declared constraints permit returned advisory fixed versions

title: Affected advisory publication age is within 30 days

title: Reported latest package releases are within 24 months
review_note: Latest-release recency is a maintenance signal; old stable releases may still be supported. Explain provider freshness and avoid a proven-vulnerability claim.

title: Reported source repositories remain available and active
review_note: Repository availability/activity is a supply-chain signal, not proof of installed code exploitability or vendor support.

title: No wildcard constraints in composer.json
review_note: Wildcard constraints concern future dependency resolution policy; deployed lockfile risk needs separate advisory/version evidence. Review high severity.

title: No dev branches in composer.json
review_note: Dev constraints are risk indicators; pinned commit/package context matters. Review blanket high severity.

title: prefer-stable=true in composer.json
review_note: prefer-stable is dependency-resolution policy, not a production vulnerability by itself. Review blanket high severity.

title: Direct locked versions match the reported latest stable release

title: Direct named query methods use a literal first argument
review_note: Named query/exec receiver may not be a database; literal arguments do not prove binding or absence of SQL injection. Keep strict policy optional; report observed construct as candidate.

title: No unconditional validateForCsrf acceptance override
review_note: Unconditional validateForCsrf acceptance is useful review evidence; bind to actual controller/interface/route before claiming a request can bypass protection.

title: Custom source avoids enumerated native network primitives
review_note: Native network primitives include file_get_contents local reads. It is an optional coding policy signal, not proof of SSRF.

title: Custom source avoids native unserialize calls
review_note: Native unserialize call is a useful sink signal; impact depends on input control, options and reachable classes. Do not demand replacement solely to silence a safe use.

title: Custom source avoids enumerated shell/process primitives
review_note: Shell/process calls need input/reachability context; they are not automatically command injection. Retain file/line and safe remediation.

title: Custom source avoids eval and create_function constructs
review_note: eval/create_function constructs are useful dynamic execution candidates; reachability and argument control determine risk.

title: Custom source avoids enumerated raw filesystem primitives
review_note: Filesystem API use is normal in Magento. Keep optional policy; distinguish path control and scope before suggesting a traversal vulnerability.

title: Custom source avoids native upload move calls
review_note: move_uploaded_file does not itself bypass upload validation; show the sink and ask to inspect validation/filename/storage/execution policy.

title: Custom source avoids enumerated weak randomness APIs
review_note: Weak PRNG calls matter in security-sensitive use. Nonsecurity randomization must not be described as a token vulnerability.

title: No direct request superglobals in named log method arguments
review_note: Direct request logging is useful disclosure-risk evidence. Do not delete required audit events; redact/minimize relevant fields. Correlate broad superglobal findings.

title: Custom source avoids enumerated raw crypto and session APIs
review_note: Raw hash/crypto/session API calls can be legitimate. Keep optional policy; identify security purpose and options before changing them.

title: No enumerated XML external feature constructs in custom source
review_note: XML external-feature syntax is useful candidate evidence; input trust, resolver and runtime parser settings determine exploitability.

title: No plain HTTP standalone PHP string literals in custom source
review_note: Standalone HTTP strings include documentation/local references; keep optional policy and establish actual endpoint use before claiming insecure transport.

title: Application worker code paths are read-only
review_note: Matched worker effective-access observation is useful; report unsupported identity as collection gap, not security suspicion. Does not inventory all workers automatically.

title: Upload inventory has no configured PHP or handler signatures
review_note: PHP/handler signatures are useful suspicious-file candidates. False positives and execution configuration need triage; correlate MB-0780.

title: Direct global Admin ACL grants match the approved role policy
review_note: Unexpected direct global ACL grant is an observed policy violation; full business least privilege is not proven.

title: Named checkout response emits the explicit enforced CSP baseline
review_note: Strict checkout CSP baseline may reject deliberately used sources. Distinguish observed header policy deviation from demonstrated XSS; correlate MB-0779 without hiding distinct directives.

title: Observed application response emits nosniff
review_note: Useful scoped production observation. Keep concrete target/config/path evidence and requirement-specific remediation; distinguish the exact observed deviation from exploitability.

title: Named integration debug settings resolve disabled in default scope
review_note: Integration debug flag default-scope observation is useful but not every store/worker runtime. Missing input is a collection gap.

title: Collected Composer dependency sources match explicit policy
review_note: Source/revision mismatch is a supply-chain policy deviation, not proof of malicious package. Missing baseline is collection context.

title: Declared mitigation records satisfy structure and expiry policy
review_note: Keep as operational readiness; Record structure/expiry belongs to operational readiness, not proof a mitigation is applied or ineffective. Consider readiness lane or supplement the original vulnerability. Do not label availability/performance symptoms as confirmed security vulnerabilities.

title: Configured PHP-FPM workers have no mapped Xdebug binary module
review_note: Loaded Xdebug binary is useful production-risk evidence; it does not prove remote debugging is enabled or exploitable.
